title: The admin app tells owners to message MettleUp on WhatsApp but never gives a number or a button
what: When Branding cannot save because the server step is missing, the owner reads 'Message MettleUp on WhatsApp to switch it on'. Branches, entry machines and trainer pages say the same. Nowhere in the admin app is MettleUp's WhatsApp number or a WhatsApp button, so the owner has no way to follow the line. Other screens send owners to Help and feedback instead, so the paths do not agree. The Branding case is also a fault for every gym (a missing server step), not a per-gym switch, and nobody at MettleUp is told it happened.
expected: Every 'contact MettleUp' line leads somewhere the owner can tap: Help and feedback, or a WhatsApp button with the real number. A missing server step is reported to MettleUp, not left to the owner.
fix_line: Change these lines to point at Help and feedback (or add a real WhatsApp button), and report the missing server step

title: When saving the gym look fails for an unknown reason, nobody at MettleUp ever hears of it
what: A failed Branding save or 'Use MettleUp's look' shows 'That didn't save. Please try again.' The real error is not written to the log and is not sent as a crash report, because the error is caught on the screen. If saves start failing for many gyms, MettleUp only learns when an owner complains.
expected: An unexpected save failure is logged and sent to MettleUp's crash reports (without personal data), so support can see and fix it.
fix_line: Log the real error and send it as a crash report before showing the calm message

title: A replaced or removed gym logo stays public on our server for ever
what: Every logo upload is saved as a new picture with a new name. Changing the logo, removing it, or going back to MettleUp's look only drops the link; the old picture stays public at its old address with a one-year cache. The confirm box says it 'removes your logo'. Only deleting the whole gym from HQ cleans logos up.
expected: An old logo is deleted from our server when the gym replaces or removes it, or the words say it is only taken off the app.
fix_line: Delete the previous logo file when a new look is saved or cleared

title: Every saved gym logo link names one database project, so moving to a new one breaks all logos
what: Logos and product photos are saved with the database company's own project address written into the link, and the server accepts only that address. If MettleUp ever has to move to a new project (account lost, project closed, region move), every gym's saved logo link points at the old place and there is no written way to rewrite them.
expected: Saved picture links use MettleUp's own address (or a path only), so a project move does not break them; or a written move plan says how links are rewritten.
fix_line: Save picture paths, not full project links, or write the move plan

title: The admin app still relies on the founder's personal web address
what: The admin app treats two addresses as its own: the MettleUp one and an old address on the founder's personal domain, which the code says 'stays for good'. Desks that saved the old address keep using it. If that personal domain lapses or is lost, those desks stop working, and the code gives no end date or plan to move them.
expected: Only MettleUp-owned addresses carry the admin app; the old personal address forwards to the new one with a set end date.
fix_line: Forward the old address to the MettleUp one and set a date to drop it

title: The Branding help article skips half the screen
what: The help article walks through upload logo, brand colour, headings and save. It never mentions the colour suggested from the logo, 'Use my own background tone', the 'Easy to read?' check, 'Remove logo' or the free tip for logos with a photo behind them, so an owner asking about those gets no help article.
expected: The help article names every part of the Branding screen in the order the owner sees it.
fix_line: Add the missing parts to the Branding help article
